summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with abdominal pain and reported confusion after stopping ciprofloxacin due to nausea and diarrhea. Evaluation revealed no signs of active infection—afebrile, normal white blood cell count, negative blood cultures, and no bacteremia. A positive urine culture showed Enterococcus and yeast, but these were interpreted as colonization rather than infection, consistent with his chronic indwelling catheter. He developed transient acute kidney injury, likely due to dehydration or antibiotic effects, which improved with supportive care. His mental status was normal on admission, and no infectious source was confirmed. Antibiotics were discontinued after one dose of IV Zosyn. He was discharged home stable with follow-up planned with his PCP and urologist, with instructions to avoid unnecessary antibiotics and maintain hydration.
